paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take home. Some of the people in Israel were longing for the Day of the LORD, but Amos warns them, "It will be darkness and not light." (Amos 5:18) Wanting God to show up is a good thing. But if I'm wanting Him to show up while I ignore what He's already said, I'm not ready for the knock at the door. I think I'd be the guy standing there with a tray of burnt cookies, saying "Surprise, I brought snacks!"

Look at what the LORD says about their feasts, offerings and songs. He says, "I hate, I despise your feasts!" (Amos 5:21) That's STRONG. And I think the point is this: the worship wasn't the problem, because He had asked them for it. The problem is that He wants the heart behind it. He tells them, "But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream." (Amos 5:24) Not a puddle. Not a trickle on Sunday. A river that doesn't quit.

So the question for you and me is simple. Does my worship and my daily life point the same direction? God asks for songs and offerings, and He also asks for justice and righteousness in how I treat people. Amos 5:26 shows what happens when other things get the throne, and the LORD says, "Therefore I will send you into exile" (Amos 5:27). I keep my ovens ready for the Marriage Supper, and I want my whole life ready too, not just the part that sings. This isn't the end of the teaching, friend, so stay with me.
